summary:
This brief is built on the 2026-10-23T19:37:31Z fact layer, which is 15:37 ET — about 23 minutes before the NYSE close — so it is a late-session snapshot rather than a settled close: the US legs are the 2026-10-23 session up to that cut, the 11 A-share names are the 2026-10-23 close (15:00 Beijing), crypto is a 24 hour reading, and commodities are live quotes against the prior settlement. Vintages come first: the macro block is uneven — rates stop at 2026-10-21 (10Y 5.13), credit and VIX at 2026-10-22 (HY OAS 3.4, VIX 19.03), FX at 2026-10-16 — so no rates statement here is a statement about today's yields.

Today was an uneven repair. The 22 sector and theme rows closed 15 up and 7 down with a mean of 0.4070 and a median of 0.2561, but the gains sat on the software side: cybersecurity 3.2876, cloud computing 1.8926, enterprise software 1.6326 and AI software 1.5689, while AI hardware kept leaking — data centers -0.8518, AI infrastructure -0.6573, and fintech -1.7298 as the weakest row. The 5 US watchlist names averaged 0.6667 but with a median of -0.0742: MU 2.3246 and AMD 1.6902 carried the mean while NVDA -0.2733, AVGO -0.0742 and TSLA -0.3337 still traded lower. A-shares went the other way entirely — all 11 names rose, mean 3.3027, median 3.0720, with the memory chain up 7.9345 for 688825 and 5.5104 for 603986.

The composite risk score is 63.18, still high_risk, with confidence at 0.9158 (data quality 1.0, coverage 0.93, consistency 0.7191). The regime flipped from risk_on to late_cycle on cross-asset 0.625 and VIX 19.03, but neither input was generated today: the VIX value is the 2026-10-22 close, and within the 8 cross-asset inputs the dollar at 121.4048 above 105 and the real rate at 2.76 above 1.5 are level thresholds that stay lit structurally. The flip therefore reads more like a stale VIX print landing plus structural signals than a same-day confirmation of intraday risk.

trend_1d prints 2.22, but that is an intraday difference against the earlier 60.96 row generated the same calendar day; against 63.00 from the previous session it is only 0.18, so the composite is essentially flat across sessions. trend_1w 0.67 and trend_1m 15.39 are the honest one-week and one-month slopes.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation is 0.625 — 5 of 8 production signals triggered — contributing 9.375, still the model's largest single source after the 0.8 proxy discount. Within the 5, the dollar index at 121.4048 above 105 and the real rate at 2.76 above 1.5 are level thresholds that stay lit while rates and the dollar sit high; the incremental part is equity and crypto: SPY -0.4568 on the day, Bitcoin -0.2059, small caps behind by -8.7444 percentage points.

HY OAS is 3.4, wider by 0.13 from the prior 3.27 print, at the 85.62 percentile and contributing 6.8496; IG at 0.89 also edged wider, making credit the only slow variable that kept deteriorating today, with liquidity_credit at 73.76 and a rising trend. The 97.59 score attached to a reverse repo balance of 0.2 is the neutral-direction absolute-deviation mapping, not a liquidity seizure — the Fed balance sheet at 6753604.0 million dollars contracted only slightly.

The real rate is 2.76 at the 98.64 percentile and the 10Y nominal sits at 5.13 in the 98.8 percentile, a combined 9.8115 contribution; but both vintages are 2026-10-21 while the news layer has the 10Y back near 5 today, so the macro score of 74.55 describes levels two to three sessions old and must not be read as today's yield.

VIX rose from 16.68 to 19.03, lifting the volatility dimension to 36.97 with a rising trend and a 4.8448 contribution; but realized volatility is only 9.714, so the implied-to-realized gap says fear was repriced before price action followed. The VIX vintage is 2026-10-22 and today's print is missing, which is this dimension's largest uncertainty.

Equity structure at 69.35 was not repaired by today's bounce: only 0.3935 of names sit above their MA200 (61 of 155), new highs run 0.0192 (3 names) against new lows at 0.1603 (25 of 156), with small caps -8.7444 and semis -10.1531 percentage points behind. Indices and software rose; the internals did not.

supporting_signals.claim: The bounce was rotation, not repair: 15 of the 22 rows rose and 7 fell, but the gains sat in software (cybersecurity 3.2876, cloud computing 1.8926, enterprise software 1.6326, AI software 1.5689), the weakest rows were fintech -1.7298 and gaming -1.1407, and AI hardware kept falling with data centers -0.8518 and AI infrastructure -0.6573.

Energy is today's hardest macro input: WTI at 103.48 (4.0314), Brent settling at 116.72 (3.14 per the CLS wire) and copper at 6.498 (2.1297), while gold fell -1.2314. Crude running up into inflation expectations is the real reason the macro score of 74.55 refuses to fall; commodities carry no evidence entry in the current fact layer, so this claim is directional only.

The inflation chain is repricing: CPI 3.71725 against a prior 3.35302, core CPI 2.56584 against 2.44616, core PCE 3.0076, while the latest payrolls print was only 29.0 thousand (prior 133.0) with unemployment at 4.2. Weaker growth into sticky inflation is the fundamental footnote under the late_cycle call.

There is no policy cushion: the reverse repo balance at 0.2 is near zero, SOFR is 3.9, and FedWatch implies 4.04 with the direction flagged as hike, so the market has not priced easing into the 10-28 FOMC meeting.

Crypto lent no risk-appetite confirmation: Bitcoin at 81185.0 (-0.2059) and Ethereum at 2392.92 (0.30859) merely moved sideways with dominance at 0.594269, so btc_down stays lit in the cross-asset block.

contradicting_signals.claim: Semis were the epicentre of the previous session and stopped falling today: semis 0.9168, semiconductors 0.6433, equipment 0.882, with MU 2.3246 and AMD 1.6902. On hardware alone, today was a repair day, not a worse one.

A-shares diverged from the US: all 11 names rose, mean 3.3027 and median 3.0720, with 688825 up 7.9345 and 603986 up 5.5104. Global risk appetite is not uniformly impaired, and a buyback wave on the A-share side (news layer) is an independent prop.

Realized volatility at 9.714 sits far below VIX 19.03. Historically that gap closes either through a lower VIX or through higher realized vol; if it is the former, the score lacks fuel to push higher.
Credit levels remain low in absolute terms: HY OAS 3.4 is still far from the 4 trigger threshold and IG is 0.89, while gold fell and copper rose, so there is no broad haven-driven de-risking.

The trend dimension is still mild: the price sits 4.6026 percentage points above MA200, the 52 week drawdown is only -2.39 and 3 month momentum is 2.8927, so the medium-term index structure is intact.

what_changed_today: The regime flipped from risk_on to late_cycle on cross-asset 0.625 at or above 0.55 together with VIX 19.03 at or above 18.

The cross-asset trigger count fell from 6 to 5 and confirmation from 0.75 to 0.625: copper swung from -2.2161 to 2.1297, switching copper_down off; gold was negative on both days, so gold_up never lit.
VIX rose from 16.68 to 19.03 and lifted the volatility dimension from 26.53 in the previous session to 36.97 with a rising trend.
Sector leadership rotated from AI hardware into software: cybersecurity 3.2876 and cloud computing 1.8926 led, while data centers -0.8518 and AI infrastructure -0.6573 kept falling.
The 22 rows closed 15 up and 7 down, mean 0.4070 and median 0.2561, the mirror image of the previous session's one-way decline.

The composite at 63.18 is essentially flat against 63.00 from the previous session (0.18); trend_1d 2.22 is an intraday difference against the earlier 60.96 row generated the same calendar day, not a session-to-session change.
Energy repriced: WTI 103.48 (4.0314) and Brent 116.72 added fresh fuel to the inflation-expectations chain.
All 11 A-share names rose with a mean of 3.3027, widening the divergence from the US median of -0.0742.
watch_next: The 10-28 FOMC is next week's single largest event: FedWatch implies 4.04 with the direction flagged as hike and the 10Y pinned near 5, so policy and rates carry the highest combined sensitivity.
Earnings season clusters: 10-26 VZ, 10-27 BA, HCA, HOOD, KO, PYPL, SOFI and V, 10-28 ETSY, F, FDX, GOOGL, MGM and MSFT, 10-29 AMZN, CARR, COIN, INTC and PINS.
The rates vintage must catch up to 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 on the next trading day, otherwise the macro dimension's rates leg keeps lagging by two sessions.
Oil: Brent at 116.72 is already a 6 month high with Hormuz and Iran risk unresolved; a further run would press inflation expectations and HY OAS at the same time.
Breadth: whether the new-low ratio can retreat from 0.1603 and whether the above-MA200 share can stop falling from 0.3935 is the test of this bounce's quality.
Whether the semis relative gap of -10.1531 percentage points narrows; only then does equity_structure at 69.35 have room to repair.
The FX vintage sits at 2026-10-16, 3 trading sessions behind rates, so any read on the dollar at 121.4048 needs a discount.

bull_case.title: Bull case: VIX retreats and breadth repairs
points: If VIX returns below 18 and the new-low ratio retreats from 0.1603, the regime has the ingredients to fall back to risk_on.
Continued repair in semis (semis 0.9168 and equipment 0.882 today) can pull the semis relative gap back from -10.1531.

base_case.title: Base case: sideways near 63 with high_risk intact
points: The composite oscillates between 60 and 70 while leadership keeps rotating between software and hardware.
Until the rates vintage catches up, the macro dimension at 74.55 is unlikely to fall meaningfully.

bear_case.title: Bear case: credit and oil resonate, score tests 70
points: If HY OAS moves from 3.4 through the 4 trigger threshold, the cross-asset count returns above 6 and the score has room to test 70.
Brent holding 116.72 would push inflation expectations and credit spreads higher together, a self-reinforcing pressure loop.
